summary: The source diagnosis for the first mismatch is complete. The ordinary Wisdom exercise in read.c::seffects() matches: the bounded replay observed JS exerciseAttribute(A_WIS, true) at RNG index 2709 with moves=1, AEXE(WIS)=0, ACURR(WIS)=12, consuming rn2(19)=5. C’s additional rn2(19)=7 at index 2710 is also owned by attrib.c::exercise(), but is caused by discovery during controlled teleportation: teleport.c::scrolltele() calls read.c::learnscroll() before getpos(); learnscrolltyp() calls makeknown() for an unknown scroll; the makeknown macro reaches o_init.c::discover_object(), whose credit_hero branch calls exercise(A_WIS, TRUE). JS teleport.js::scrolltele() omits learnscroll() in its wizard-controlled branch; its later call follows the branch, and successful getpos()/teleds() returns before reaching it. The actionable whole-function scope is teleport.c::scrolltele(). A separate step-51 getpos()/teleds() screen and cursor mismatch remains unresolved: C cursor [26,16,1], JS [48,0,1], with row 0 column 40 space versus hyphen.

source.branch: Whole-function scope: scrolltele() (teleport.c:849-915). In the wizard-controlled branch, C calls learnscroll(scroll) at teleport.c:883-884 before getpos(). For this unknown scroll, the full consumed path is read.c::learnscroll() → learnscrolltyp() → makeknown() (hack.h:1530 macro) → o_init.c::discover_object(); the latter credits Wisdom at o_init.c:480-483. The earlier generic exercise remains read.c::seffects() at 2199-2200. JS scrolltele() lacks the pre-getpos learnscroll call in its controlled branch, and successful destination selection returns before its later fallback learnscroll call.
callers: read.c::seffect_teleportation() dispatches an uncursed, unconfused teleport scroll to scrolltele(); read.c::seffects() first performs the generic Wisdom exercise for a magic scroll at read.c:2199-2200.

teleport.c::scrolltele() calls read.c::learnscroll() at lines 883-884 before getpos() in the wizard/controlled branch; read.c::learnscroll() calls learnscrolltyp(), which calls makeknown() when oc_name_known is false.
hack.h:1530 expands makeknown(x) to discover_object(x, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE); o_init.c::discover_object() calls exercise(A_WIS, TRUE) at line 483 when it newly marks a type known and credit_hero is true.

Production wiring: read.c::seffect_teleportation() calls scrolltele() for an uncursed, unconfused teleport scroll (read.c:2021-2030); JS js/read.js::seffect_teleportation() awaits scrolltele() at line 2057, after js/read.js::seffects() performs the generic Wisdom exercise.
dependencies: attrib.c::exercise(): rejects only INT/CHA, non-Wisdom polymorph exercise, and abs(AEXE(i)) >= 50; on the increasing branch it consumes rn2(19), compares against ACURR(i), and changes AEXE(i) only if the roll is greater.

AEXE(WIS) is u.aexe.a[A_WIS] and ACURR(WIS) is acurr(A_WIS) (include/attrib.h:23-24). The bounded JS trace observed AEXE=0 and ACURR=12 before the matching seffects draw; rn2(19)=5 does not increment AEXE, so the next C discovery exercise can draw with the same values.
read.c::learnscrolltyp() only invokes makeknown() while objects[scrolltyp].oc_name_known is false, then calls more_experienced(0, 10); read.c::learnscroll() skips spellbooks.
o_init.c::discover_object() updates the discovery list and knowledge flags, credits exercise(A_WIS, TRUE) only when a previously unknown type is marked known, then updates inventory during live play.

JS teleport.js::scrolltele() calls learnscroll() only after the control-flow block. Its successful controlled getpos()/teleok()/teleds() path returns early, unlike C, which learns the scroll before getpos().
The later getpos()/teleds() cursor and output difference at step 51 is a separate unresolved trace; it is not attributed to the missing discovery draw.

evidence: .cache/synthetic-scans/v15/wizard-uncursed-scroll-teleports-within-level.json and the C recording challenges/cases/v15/wizard-uncursed-scroll-teleports-within-level.session.json preserve the original one-screen mismatch, provenance, and step trace; step 45 has rn2(19)=5 @ exercise and step 46 has rn2(19)=7 @ exercise.

One bounded instrumented JS replay completed as run-2pTwiE (receipt/log directory /tmp/teleport-validation-1000/run-2pTwiE). It observed one exerciseAttribute call for the generic seffects draw at RNG index 2709, with index=A_WIS, increase=true, moves=1, AEXE=0, ACURR=12; no JS exercise call or RNG draw follows at index 2710. The replay reproduces the same final screen and cursor mismatch.

Frozen C source at commit 6d2c675aad59f170ec44980d6afce47f08ae7423: read.c:2199-2200 gives the generic seffects exercise; teleport.c:883-884 calls learnscroll before getpos; read.c:58-76 defines learnscrolltyp()/learnscroll(); hack.h:1530 maps makeknown() to discover_object(); o_init.c:480-483 performs the second credited Wisdom exercise.

Frozen JS source at the same commit: js/teleport.js::scrolltele() has no learnscroll() in its wizard-controlled branch, and its successful controlled branch returns from getpos()/teleok()/teleds() before the bottom fallback learnscroll() call. js/read.js::learnscrolltyp() and js/o_init.js::discover_object() otherwise contain the matching discovery/exercise path.

The remaining step-51 output/cursor mismatch is still recorded separately in the original mismatch object: C cursor [26,16,1], JS cursor [48,0,1], and C space versus JS hyphen at row 0 column 40 after key ".". Its getpos()/teleds() cause has not been attributed.
